scope: Third-order deductions from the unchanged EdgeBench v1 theory, official public Codex configuration, and fixed science task contracts. All experiment designs are Frontier-Science proposals, not EdgeBench empirical results.
source_facts: The EdgeBench theory assumes that raw interaction time supplies search effort approximately linearly and notes that characteristic feedback cycles can invalidate one log-time coordinate.
The official public Codex configuration uses a 43200-second horizon and 1800-second observer auto-evaluation interval for all 51 listed tasks.
The 51 official public Codex task settings have submission-cooldown counts 44 at 120 seconds, 3 at 216 seconds, 1 at 2160 seconds, and 3 at 0 seconds.

The theory identifies weighted cut mixing and approximately self-similar edge-difficulty growth as sufficient ingredients for the frontier interpretation, and predicts chains, modules and bottlenecks as non-logistic failure modes.
EdgeBench tasks specify their objective, deliverables and judge before the run; the released benchmark does not report an open scientific-question formulation experiment.

The public Borden contract requires a legal baseline workflow, while the D-ABIC contract specifies a published method and comparison route; these contracts motivate but do not themselves quantify starter-prior anchoring.

frontier_science_experiments.design: Hold active compute, local calls, total authoritative feedback events and bits, and confirmation budget fixed while randomizing immediate, evenly spaced, batched, jittered and end-only release schedules.

Generate answer-disjoint procedural twins with matched marginal scientific work-unit difficulty, score mass, feedback and cost but well-mixed, chain, modular-single-bridge and hierarchical dependency graphs; randomize bridge or prerequisite availability.
Compare author-fixed, candidate-menu and open preregistered question contracts in one rich procedural laboratory before outcome-bearing data are released.
Randomize blank schema-only, quality-matched neutral, development-plausible wrong, correct and diverse-choice executable starters on identical procedural worlds.

claim_boundary: No new EdgeBench numerical performance result is claimed.
The cooldown census is a fact about the official public Codex configuration, not evidence that it changes EdgeBench headline curves.
Until S4 is run, Frontier-Science should not call a wall-time slope an agent-intrinsic scientific learning rate.
Until S5 is run, a log-sigmoid fit should not be presented as empirical validation of the latent task-graph mechanism.
Until Q1 and K3 are run, fixed-objective performance should not be called research-agenda formation or starter-independent method discovery.
